correctness.rationale: The positive quadratic gives a proper global first integral and unique energy circles. The exact time integral uses both velocity branches, and substitution t=K(v) makes its asymptotic moments finite: F(t) grows at most t^-1/2 near zero and decays exponentially at infinity. Taylor expansion with second-moment domination and exponentially negligible endpoint tail establishes the full O(A^-5) period remainder. The angular substitution evaluates I0 and I1; the logarithmic two-sided constants of K give the velocity-extrema ratio. The analytic angular coordinate gives the already-known local coefficient, and continuity forces the asserted nonunique interior maximum. Symbolic and numerical cross-checks agree.

value.rationale: This treats the entire natural strict-discriminant global-center region, rather than a special numeric slice. The exact first correction to the inverse-amplitude physical period and the exponential asymmetry of opposite peak speeds are mathematically motivated observables that distinguish parameters within the same qualitative global-center phase portrait. Coupled with an established local coefficient, the infinity law yields a provable region with an interior maximum of the period. The correction is strictly positive for every permitted parameter, a nontrivial global constraint absent from center-existence results.
